title: The key picks the partition; the group gives each partition one reader
caption: Topic 'orders' with 3 partitions and consumer group 'billing' with 2 members. Order is kept inside a partition, never across them.

steps.text: The producer computes hash(order_id) % 3 for every record. Every event of order 17 lands in p0, in the order it was written.
Each partition is an append-only file. A record's offset (0, 1, 2…) is its permanent position in that partition.
Group 'billing' splits the partitions: c1 owns p0 and p1, c2 owns p2. Each partition has exactly one reader in the group, so per-key order survives.
Each consumer pulls from its committed offset. A third consumer would get p0 or p1 from c1; a fourth would sit idle, because there are only 3 partitions.

scenarios.name: Consumer c2 dies
scenarios.summary: The group rebalances and c1 takes over p2 from its last committed offset. Order per key survives; work since the last commit is redone.

steps.text: c2 crashes. Its heartbeats stop, and p2 has no reader.
After the session timeout the coordinator rebalances: the group now has one member, so c1 owns all three partitions. Reading p2 pauses meanwhile.
c1 starts reading p2 from the offset the group last committed for it. Anything c2 processed after that commit is processed again.
Producers never noticed: they keep writing by key, and each partition still has exactly one reader.

scenarios.name: Risk: hot partition
scenarios.summary: A skewed key (one huge tenant, one viral item) sends most traffic to one partition, and its single consumer can't keep up. Salt the key or split that traffic out.

steps.text: Order 17 belongs to a giant tenant: 90% of all records carry its key, and hash(key) % 3 sends every one of them to p0.
p0 grows much faster than the others, and only one consumer in the group may read it.
Meanwhile c2 and the other partitions are almost idle. Adding consumers doesn't help: p0 still has one reader.
Mitigation: salt the hot key (17#0 … 17#7) so it spreads over partitions, giving up strict order for that key, or move that tenant to its own topic.

scenarios.name: More consumers or partitions
scenarios.summary: Parallelism per group is capped by the partition count: a 4th consumer on 3 partitions sits idle. To scale further you need more partitions, chosen up front.

steps.text: Traffic grows, so the team scales billing from 2 to 4 consumers.
The rebalance gives each of 3 partitions to one consumer: c1, c2 and c3 now each read one.
c4 gets nothing. Two readers of one partition would break per-key order, so Kafka never does that.
The real lever is partitions. But adding them later remaps hash(key) % N and breaks per-key order across the change, so provision 2–3× the partitions you need today.
